text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The public Slovak Television (STV) and the official Slovak Radio on Monday begin an information campaign on the up coming referenda on NATO membership and direct presidential elections.

- President Michal Kovac said Slovakia had a "lower chance" to be invited to start integration talks with NATO after a July summit in Madrid. But Kovac said chances to win membership in the first wave of enlargement could increase if the ruling coalition positively reacted to western criticism.

- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said property worth some 30 billion crowns remained to be privatised to complete the privatisation process in Slovakia. Meciar said some privatisation rights would be transfered to the government in accordance with a ruling by the Constitutional Court.
- Slovakia's largest drug producer Slovakofarma has chosen Nomura International Plc to lead manage its 231 million crown GDR issue later this year.

- Deutsche Bank expects Slovak GDP to rise by about four percent year-on-year in 1997, compared with last year's 6.9 percent increaese. It should slow further to about three percent growth in 1998. The bank forecasts the unemployment rate to drop to 11.5 percent this year from 12.5 percent in 1996.
- Car importers said the measure requiring a deposit of 20 percent of the value of imported goods on interest-free accounts discriminates against foreign cars and will increase their prices.
- JAS Bardejov, one of the largest Slovak shoe producers, said the import deposit measure will help stabilise the company's position on the domestic market.

SME - Opposition parties said people should vote in favour of NATO membership and direct presidential elections, but that they should ignore questions on the deployment of foreign troop and nuclear weapons in Slovakia.

- Both minor partners in the ruling coaliton, the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS) and the extreme right Workers Party (ZRS), said people should vote against the integration to NATO and direct presidential elections.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The unemployment rate is expected to ease in coming months due to seasonal factors.
- Sony officially opened its television component factory in Trnava, western Slovakia, last Friday.
- The government has proposed a 10 percent increase in pensions, effective July 1, 1997.
